classification.difficultyReason: Infers rectangle dimensions from intersecting equal circles and uses Pythagoras before calculating area.

content.prompt: The two circles below have radius $2\text{ cm}$ and each passes through the centre of the other. Find the area of the rectangle indicated in the diagram.

spec.description: Two complete congruent circle outlines overlap. The shaded rectangle has horizontal sides through the circle intersections and four corners on the circle outlines. Its vertical sides lie outside the centres.
spec.mathematics: Each circle has radius 2 cm; centre separation is 2 cm. Relative to the midpoint of the centres, centres are at (-1,0) and (1,0), intersections at (0,±sqrt(3)), and rectangle corners at (±2,±sqrt(3)). Coordinates are construction data, not printed givens.
spec.answerVisibility: No centre points, lengths, auxiliary constructions or answers are printed.

answer.short:
$8\sqrt3\text{ cm}^2$.

Use Pythagoras to find the half-height $\sqrt3\text{ cm}$; the rectangle is $4\text{ cm}$ wide.
answer.worked:
Let $O_1$ and $O_2$ be the centres, $M$ their midpoint and $U$ the upper circle intersection. Since each circle passes through the other's centre, $O_1O_2=2\text{ cm}$. Symmetry gives $O_1M=1\text{ cm}$ and $MU\perp O_1O_2$.
$$\begin{align*}
MU^2&=2^2-1^2\\
MU^2&=3\\
MU&=\sqrt3\text{ cm}.
\end{align*}$$
The rectangle's height is $2\sqrt3\text{ cm}$. At the upper horizontal side, each circle extends 1 cm to either side of its centre, so the rectangle's width is $1+2+1=4\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}
A&=4\times2\sqrt3\\
A&=8\sqrt3\text{ cm}^2.
\end{align*}$$
